body.statement: Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), under independent multinomial sampling and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\) when margins are estimated, the deterministic selector \(\widehat\chi_n\) chooses an incident first-order-compatible rigid chart and \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one. On these certified separated rigid charts, \(\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)\Rightarrow N(0,V_{\tau})\), and \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\). Because \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), scalar contrasts and the elliptical branch of \(W_n\) have asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). If no chart is certified, the total procedure returns \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(\widehat\tau_n=(0,0)\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and \(W_n=[0,1]^2\), with no covariance-consistency or Wald-coverage assertion for that fallback branch.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(H\) be a compact subset of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\).  The multinomial central limit and delta result in \(\mathrm{lem:multinomial\text{-}clt\text{-}and\text{-}delta}\), applied to the selected table and to the independent margin table when present, gives uniformly on \(H\)
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}. \tag{9}
\]
The proportional-sample assumption gives the margin block multiplied by \(\lambda\); when margins are known that block is absent.  Compactness and selected-cell positivity make the required second moments and covariance maps uniformly bounded and continuous.

For every incident chart \(\chi\), \(d_{\chi}(\zeta)=0\).  The distance to a closed set is one-Lipschitz, and hence
\[
d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)
\le \|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2
=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(t_n),
\qquad t_n=n^{-1/4}. \tag{10}
\]
Continuity of the finitely many normalized slacks and \(\eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\) imply that the slack test is at least \(\varepsilon/2\) with probability tending to one, uniformly on \(H\).  Conversely, every incompatible chart closure is at distance at least \(\varepsilon\).  The triangle inequality and (9) make its empirical distance exceed \(t_n\) with probability tending to one.  Exhaustiveness of the full atlas ensures that there is no omitted chart.  Thus the selector chooses an incident first-order-compatible chart with probability tending to one.

All incident selected charts have the same value and Jacobian at \(\zeta\), and their extensions have uniformly bounded second derivative on the neighborhoods in the definition of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\).  Taylor's formula and (9) therefore give, independently of which qualifying chart is chosen,
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
=J_{\chi}(\zeta)\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+o_P(1)
\Rightarrow N(0,V_{\tau}). \tag{11}
\]
Continuity of the derivatives and of the sandwich map gives
\[
\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}
J_{\chi}(\zeta)\Omega_{\zeta}J_{\chi}(\zeta)^{\top}=V_{\tau}. \tag{12}
\]
Since \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), (12) implies positive definiteness and hence \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one.  Slutsky's lemma applied to (11)--(12) yields the standard normal limit for every nonzero scalar contrast with positive limiting variance and the \(\chi^2_2\) limit for the quadratic form defining the ellipse.  Therefore the corresponding scalar and elliptical Wald regions have asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).

If no chart qualifies, the identities \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(F_{\bot}=(0,0)\), \(J_{\bot}=0\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and \(W_n=[0,1]^2\) follow directly from the definitions.  The proof above used certification and separation and therefore makes no covariance or Wald assertion for that fallback event.
body.justification: The chart rule, covariance formula, and nonsingularity margin make regular-stratum Wald inference operational and falsifiable.
body.gap: The anchor and earlier response-type estimators establish regular-case normality only for their inverse formulas, not for deterministically selected rational and simple algebraic rigid charts.
body.consumer: Separated empirical tables obtain reproducible standard errors and Wald regions on every first-order-compatible atlas chart.
